title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: ERNIE'S BIG DANCE
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Ernie Batista, a locksmith from Providence, Rhode Island.
Ernie can open any lock in the state. But he dances like a folding chair.
And his daughter Sofia was getting married in June.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE ASK
segments.quote: The greatest mistake you can make in life is to be continually fearing you will make one.
segments.author: Elbert Hubbard
lines: Sofia said, Dad, I want a real father-daughter dance. Not the shuffle.
Ernie wanted to say no. Everyone would laugh.
Then he saw a card taped inside his toolbox, from the writer Elbert Hubbard:
The greatest mistake you can make in life is to be continually fearing you will make one.
That week, he signed up with Miss Pearl, seventy-nine, above a pizza place.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: TEN TOES
segments.quote: It is one of the blessings of old friends that you can afford to be stupid with them.
segments.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
lines: First lesson, Ernie stepped on Miss Pearl's feet eleven times. She counted.
He was too embarrassed to go back. So his wife Angie came along, quoting Ralph Waldo Emerson:
It is one of the blessings of old friends that you can afford to be stupid with them.
Thirty years married. So they were stupid together every Tuesday, and laughed all the way home.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE BROOM
segments.quote: Whether it means to learn to dance by practicing dancing or to learn to live by practicing living, the principles are the same.
segments.author: Martha Graham
lines: One hour a week was not enough. Miss Pearl had a note on her mirror, from the great dancer Martha Graham:
Whether it means to learn to dance by practicing dancing or to learn to live by practicing living, the principles are the same.
So Ernie practiced in his shop every morning, with a broom as his partner.
A customer walked in once. Ernie said, We're just friends.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE KITCHEN
segments.quote: We should consider every day lost on which we have not danced at least once.
segments.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
lines: In May, Ernie got stiff. He counted so hard, he forgot the music.
Sofia texted him a line from the German thinker Friedrich Nietzsche:
We should consider every day lost on which we have not danced at least once.
So every night, Ernie and Angie danced one song in the kitchen, between the stove and the fridge.
He stopped counting and started listening.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE TRIP
segments.quote: We cannot really love anybody with whom we never laugh.
segments.author: Agnes Repplier
lines: Then came the wedding. On the very first spin, Ernie's shoe caught the rug, and down he went.
He wanted to disappear. Then he remembered the writer Agnes Repplier:
We cannot really love anybody with whom we never laugh.
So he laughed. Sofia laughed. Two hundred guests laughed.
He got up and finished the dance. Nobody remembers the fall.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: TUESDAYS
segments.quote: We are here on Earth to fart around, and don't let anybody tell you different.
segments.author: Kurt Vonnegut
lines: After the wedding, Angie showed him a line from Kurt Vonnegut:
We are here on Earth to fart around, and don't let anybody tell you different.
So they still dance with Miss Pearl every Tuesday. Just for fun.
She says Ernie only steps on her feet twice now. She still counts.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Say yes. Be silly together. Practice. Dance daily. Laugh when you fall. Have fun.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Say yes. Be silly together. Practice. Dance every day. Laugh when you fall. Have fun.
I danced at my own wedding once. My wife still has the bruise.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
